utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I understood that you would like to address the Court for three minutes, but before giving you an opportunity to do so, I'd first ask Ms. Pilipovic, at an earlier occasion you said that the expert reports would be available early November, although I would understand early November to be somewhere in the first 10 days. It is certain that if we are after the 15th, it could not be said to be early November any more. Tomorrow is the 15th. Could you provide us with some information.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, tomorrow I will be going to Belgrade and I think that on Tuesday I will be able to provide all the expert reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's then early in the second half of November. Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, good morning. Thank you. And since we are talking about dates, this is the subject that I want to address. Yesterday we saw that the Prosecution produced a copy, a fragmented copy and with an inappropriate scale of a map, which was a corps map. The reason for my intervention is the following: First of all, we were not informed that this is how the Prosecution would proceed, and secondly, having examined this map when we returned to our homes, so to speak, we noticed, Mr. President, that all issues raised by the -- all the questions asked by the Prosecution concerned the state of a line which is outside of the time frame of the indictment. I have submitted the original of this map to the registrar who has it on her right, and I can provide copies of the legend, but unfortunately in black and white of the key. If you have a look at the third part of the key, the lower part which contains only red for the first part of this interior part. It is a dark red and a slightly lighter red, if we have a look at this map, if we open it at the part that was photocopied by the Prosecution, we will see that the questions regarded the situation of a line, the state of a line, which was on the 21st of August, 1994, which prevailed on that date. So that is after the time frame referred to in the indictment. And what is more, Mr. President, Your Honours, the first part of the key contains the yellow colour, too, and this yellow colour corresponds to the development, development of the lines, obviously, before they were fixed on this map in August 1994. I am well aware of the fact that Prosecution only received black and white copies, but the Prosecution knows, because we have seen many of these maps, the Prosecution knows that these maps always have keys which are in colour, and the Prosecution also knows, since I have written about this to them many times, perhaps in an archaic language, but nevertheless, I did write to them. They know that we are at disposition the of the Prosecution for any problems that may arise as a result. If a map is provided without the key, Mr. President, and without trying to check what the legend -- what the key is and informing you of this, we consider that this isn't an example of the best possible type of cooperation between the parties. Nevertheless, we want to show via this map that all of the questions asked by Mr. Ierace regarded the state of a line which was outside the period of the indictment, the period referred to in the indictment. And that is August 1994. This is something that we didn't know at the time because we weren't able to remember, to have all these maps in our memory. There were hundreds of them, perhaps. But everything that was done, everything that was asked with regard to this line, ought to be subject to modifications. It should quite simply be deleted from the transcript. And also, Mr. President, if we were told that these lines, even if this is a document of ours, that these lines referred to such a time frame, we would have immediately objected and I am sure that we have saved precious time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Ierace, is there any reason to respond at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I haven't seen the coloured map so it is very difficult for me to respond. I haven't seen the coloured map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Perhaps you look at it, yes, perhaps now and not...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is an issue which needs to be settled before cross-examination is concluded, and I will need the assistance of a member of my team who is not here and who is not a lawyer. I respectfully seek a 10-minute adjournment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before adjourning, Mr. Ierace, could you tell the Chamber what issues you had still in mind, because we asked yesterday an assessment of the -- and perhaps, if we would adjourn we could use that minutes to consider that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I would resist the suggestion that the time taken for me to respond to this should come out of my cross-examination. I can tell you that before this issue was raised, I intended to take only a few minutes, but that may now change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn for 10 minutes. --- Break taken at 9.12 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, first of all, I indicated that you would get 10 minutes, but the Chamber needed some time itself as well to start considering the submissions made by Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might I have access to the map. I think it is with the accused at the moment. Mr. President, with your leave, I'd like the map to be placed on the board so that the Trial Chamber can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: This will take just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We might ask the Defence to look closer to the map at a later stage as well, but let's first put it on the board.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. President, it would save time if Mr. Mundis could point out certain features as I speak. I anticipate I will take no more than two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whilst it is being prepared, I reiterate, we have received only a black and white copy. On the top left-hand corner, the map is expressed to indicate the date which is the 1st of July 1994. When one goes to the bottom left-hand corner one sees a legend. The first entry, as I understand it, effectively translates as confrontation lines and the three colours are indicated yellow red and blew. When one looks at the relevant part of the confrontation line which was a subject of evidence yesterday, we see the same three colours. If one goes back to the legend, one see a second group of colours indicated confrontation lines as of the date of the 3rd of August, 1994. None of those colours relate to the part of the confrontation line which was the subject of yesterday's evidence. They relate to parts of the confrontation line outside Sarajevo. The third and last entry in the legend is again a separate group of colours, indicating according to the legend, confrontation line as of the 21st of August, 1994. That third group of colours also relates to a different part of the confrontation line, not the part we were concerned with yesterday. In other words, to the extent the document speaks for itself, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. where there were changes after the 1st of July, 1994, to the confrontation line, those positions are indicated. None of the changes relate to the part of the confrontation line which was the subject of evidence yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would just like to approach the map because I think one needs good glasses to see it. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand what the Prosecution says, Mr. President. I am not an expert in this field, in maps and keys. The only thing that I can establish which is incontestable is that in one version, as well as in the other, there is a yellow area which is still indicated. We can see from a distance. Around these lines and which corresponds, if I understand it correctly, to the area of the establishment of the line, at the start of the conflict, and the first date indicated in the key, which is, more or less, July 1994. And in the copy that the Prosecution handed to us with this witness, through the witness, the yellow area did not appear and, therefore, the witness was somewhat, not misled, but he was in a situation where he couldn't really see the map properly because he lacked this area. And I think that this area, the yellow area, which is the area where the lines moved, is an important element. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that what my learned colleague has just said needs to be corrected. The significance of the yellow, it is apparent from the map, is only to better indicate the position of the confrontation lines themselves, which are indicated in the colours red and blue. The yellow appears behind the red confrontation line. In other words, from the red confrontation line radiating away under that side of the confrontation line. Essentially what we have here is a map made as of the 1st of July 1994 which was updated as the line changed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like this map to be produced in evidence, the original one, so that we have the map always in its right context and that all colours can be seen clearly on the map that is in evidence, so that we don't have to work with black and white copies or with bad copies. And I think we are at a point where the -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have a problem here. We did not wish to tender this map for a number of reasons, or rather we wanted to tender it but we couldn't because it was impossible for us to copy this kind of document, and we needed to continue to work with our witnesses and we can see how difficult it is to work on black and white documents, people get lost and can't find their bearings and so on. If we only have segments that's not going to be enough. It is a little bit of a technical problem. We don't know how to copy this kind of thing in a necessary format.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... That a coloured copy will be available to the Defence so that they can further prepare for, that's for sure, and that's a technical problem, and we will have to solve that. I think that's fair to the Defence because without a good copy of this map, they might have difficulties in repairing for the presentation of their case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the problem is of the format, of the size. I think special equipment is necessary. I don't think that's commercially available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Special equipment or someone that -- I see that even this map is already with some tape on it, and then to reconstruct the map in such a way that it can be -- it can be used for the preparation of the Defence. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I would be grateful if the Defence could now clearly indicate whether they accept that the confrontation lines on the relevant part of this map, that is, in relation to the parts the subject of cross-examination yesterday, are according to this map as they were on the 1st of July 1994. I would be grateful for that before I continue cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will reply to the question. No. No, for two reasons and the first reason is the scale that I have calculated on this map, what the thickness of the lines is, whatever the colour. One of the line is about 80 metres. I have spoken to witnesses and even 80 to 90 metres, witnesses say it is a question of life and death in combat. The second reason is this: That corps maps -- Mr. Ierace, just let me finish, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It is a misunderstanding, Mr. President, which may save time. I am not talking about the black and white map. In relation to this coloured map, does the Defence now say --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I have just answered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... About the copy in front of us. You were explaining that you would not accept the lines to indicate with sufficient precision or at all, the confrontation line, as they existed on the 1st of July 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The second reason is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please tell us the reason. Although the most important thing is that you do not accept them. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, no, because we did not wish to produce, to tender this map. And if the Prosecution wish to have this map entered as a document, I will explain. The second reason is that corps maps are less detailed in the information that they give compared to the battalion maps. Corps maps give a very general view of the problem, and they are, therefore, less precise as to what is known on the level of the battalion. This is the reason why I said "no." These are the two reasons, although I have been interrupted, I have managed to state this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you say that there are maps more precise, I think you are always in a position to tender them into evidence, and I would like to add one thing. The differences between the markings on the other map the witness did last Monday, I think it was, the difference is with those markings and the confrontation lines as they appear on this map with whatever position, is an issue that came up in cross-examination, and, of course, could be the subject for re-examination, if the Defence would like to do so. Then I think we are at a point where we could -- yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just one remaining matter, Mr. President. Mr. Piletta-Zanin has referred to battalion maps. He has not given them to the Prosecution. If he has them he is required to do so under the rules of reciprocal disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have battalion maps, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I said earlier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just asking you a question, whether you have battalion maps; yes or no, and then perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have them. But may I then ask you, you said that these are more precise. What then is the source of your information?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Militarily service in the Swiss Army a fortnight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand that you say battalion maps in the Swiss Army are more precise than the corps maps and that makes you -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. okay, if that is it, then it's clear to me. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is my personal military experience as well as that of the general who was able to tell me this. But everyone knows that maps on the level of the battalion are more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But we -- they are not available to us. I know Judges that confiscate mobile telephones. Since it is not in the Statute nor in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you need any technical assistance how to switch off your mobile, I will gladly assist you for the future. I hope you don't have to answer the call. Then we are at a point where we could --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, but might the map be taken down first, before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And to save time, for the benefit of Madam Registrar, I will be shortly asking that the witness be shown Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the map should not be given to the Prosecution at this very moment. But it is clear to the Defence, we'll have to solve the practical problem and the map remains to be -- you also could give it to the Registrar so that we together find a technical solution for the copying of the maps since the Chamber, it is the ruling of the Chamber that it should be produced in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And indeed, Mr. President, since we are not sitting tomorrow or Monday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Today might be a good time for it to go to the Registry for it to be copied. I simply offer that. Yes, Mr. President, I will shortly be showing the witness Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the final copying may have to be done somewhere else, and that perhaps we will look at it whether a provisional copy of parts could be made at this very moment. But this size cannot be handled in its entirety by the Tribunal, as far as I understand. But we will take proper care of that. Perhaps during the first break we will find out about what can be done today so that -- so if the map could then be put in the hands of the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only problem is that, as you know, we are sometimes working during the weekend, and this is a long weekend because we have Friday off and we need this map so that we can work with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... We will have to see whether there are -- whether we can make provisional copies for the short term, and a copy of the map in its entirety at the long run. And if you would indicate -- because I do not know what parts of the map you would specifically like to work on with your future witnesses, that if you could give some guidance to the Registrar what are, at least, the parts that you would need immediately, that would certainly assist the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, practically speaking, it would be useful for us to have the entire map. This is just for practical and technical reasons, because when we ask someone what they know they saw, for instance, on Hum, it would be important the person could tell us the distances, the ranges, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... And we will do our utmost best. Then, Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom again. Mr. Ierace, could you give us an indication as to how much time you would still need? A couple of minutes or...?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown D1789.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just first -- good morning, Mr. DP20. If this court says 9.00, it is sometimes 10.00. We had to deal with a procedural issue, but I thank you for your patience. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness, the other day you were asked by the Defence some questions about some settlements. Please place -- please look at the map when it is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At this stage we only have a black screen, Mr. President. Yes, thank you. And could we see in greater enlargement the portion of the map immediately above the name "Sarajevo" which is in bold type. If you can manipulate the map. Thank you. That will do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to point out on the map some of those settlements, first of all, Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can the map please be moved so that Sedrenik is more to the centre. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take the blue pen and underline the name "Sedrenik" on the map, which is where you have pointed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps a bit bolder. Underline it again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were also asked some questions in relation to Kobilja Glava. Would you point to the position of Kobilja Glava on the map, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you underline Kobilja Glava.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked some questions about Slatina. Can you find Slatina on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This feature, this locality is unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that the other day you were asked what the distance was between Slatina and Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember, but I didn't answer because at that time I didn't know what locality that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you say: "Well, Slatina and Sedrenik, Slatina is closer, it is closer in relation to Kobilja Glava, perhaps 1 to 2.000 metres, as the crow flies, isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. I didn't speak about Slatina because it is unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you look at the map above Kobilja Glava, do you see the name "Slatina"? Do you see that? Yes. Would you underline that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Kromolj, do you see Kromolj on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Underline that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Zuc on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it can be seen here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Zuc further to the left? In other words, beyond the lefthand boundary of the map, and, therefore, unseen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Mr. Piletta-Zanin is there Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in fact there is. If that's possible, could we have the map in colour so that the witness can have a look at it with the assistance of the usher, please. [In English] Map to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we going to fold it to the part on which we have the excerpt or do you want the whole map? Because then we have to put it on the...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I would like to present the area that we are interested in, that is the area around Sedrenik, that is the area, the segment that was photocopied. But perhaps I could do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would determine the exact portion, then we could try to fold the map, but we have to be very careful with it because there might not be...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I say in advance that I object to any form of leading in relation to this re-examination. If I say that at the outset, my position will be clearly understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please put the map a little more to the left so that we can see the other side. That's fine. Stop there. Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the question I have for you is the following. Could you take a pointer and put it on the demarcation line, on the red demarcation line that you can see to the north of Sedrenik. No, to the north of Sedrenik. More to your left, please. More. That should be there, that's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am referring to the width of the trace of the line. Witness, given the scale of the map, the scale of the map that you should be familiar with, what does this represent in metres? What does the width of the trace represent in terms of metres, the width of the trace that you have -- of the line that you have under the pointer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question assumes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that the witness is aware of the scale of the map. As far as I know, this has not been established yet. So please first verify that there will be no confusion. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, willingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the scale of this type of map, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one to 25.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Given the scale that you have mentioned, and I am asking for an approximate figure, what does the thickness of the line, of the two red lines represent, the red line that you pointed to a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the thickness, it's about 250 metres in reality, if the line is about 5 millimeters wide.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The thickness of the line, is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The thickness, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So if I have understood your testimony correctly, the position of the line --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to leading, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Indicates that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't finished my question yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please not lead, not in this question, not in any of the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in your opinion, this way of marking the line, is it a sufficiently precise of marking a line on this type of a map; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in the way that the line is used on the scale of the map, given the scale of the map, is there a possibility of making an error, given these factors; yes or no?

utterances.text: Mr. President, I appreciate that Mr. Piletta-Zanin does not have a common law background, but that is still a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a leading question, but if the witness would say that errors are impossible or whether the witness would say that errors are possible, if you ask whether human beings can make mistakes or can make errors, whatever the answer is, it's general knowledge from everyone that sometimes errors are made by human beings. So I don't know whether the question and the answer to it would assist the Chamber greatly. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will move on to another series of questions. I accepted the remarks that Mr. Ierace made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it -- is precision more possible, is it possible to be more precise in maps that are called -- I will withdraw that. Do you know whether there are maps at the level of a battalion, whether there are battalion maps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, what is the scale used for battalion maps, if you are aware of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One to 25.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether battalion maps, maps established at the level of the battalion, do you know whether they are made in a more precise manner than maps that are established at the level of a corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you tell us how maps are made on the battalion level, who makes them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The officers who are in the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are these specialised officer whose are specially assigned to make these maps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Making maps is one of their duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us whether you know anything about the equipment used to mark maps, that is, pens or other equipment -- I do not know all the technical words for this. But filth, I think the word "filth liners" is used. Do you know anything about how this is done on both levels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please tell us how exactly it is done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A map is made when the commander of the battalion works, it is more precise, because it concentrates on a smaller part, and it is easier to make to correspond to the reality on the ground. Buildings can be marked more precisely in a smaller zone, that's why I say it is more precise. There is a lot of equipment for making maps, felt tips, 0.5 millimeters which can be used in the final phase, and the 5 millimetre felt tip which was used to make this map with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a difference on the battalion level or is that the same on the battalion level, the equipment used to mark on maps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The equipment is more or less the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With your pointer, could you concentrate on --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether we could zoom out. I don't know whether the technical booth can assist us. That's fine. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in the right-hand corner there is a site, it is a symbol, a sort of a cap with two other red symbols in the interior. Could you point to that symbol. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this question does not relate to cross-examination. The symbol does not appear on the map that was shown to the witness yesterday. And in effect, this is introducing new evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, this symbol appears in the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know what this symbol represents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It represents an anti-armoured attachment at a firing position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "an anti-armour group" there are two red symbols inside, in the interior, do you know what they represent? Could you please answer the question by saying yes or no, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. I object to leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This was to save time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know what these two symbols represent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a symbol for anti-armour weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what weapons are concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is a recoilless cannon, 82-millimetre recoilless cannon, and then anti-armour cannon, a 100-millimetre anti-armour cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Which army corps do these two weapons belong to? When you say "corps," I mean, which section, which body, which body of the army did these two weapons belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They belonged to the artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like you to examine, Witness, on the right of your screen and to the east of the word "Sarajevo" could you point to an identical symbol, on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What does this represent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same symbol. It is the symbol for an anti-armoured attachment at a firing position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, these weapons, do they belong to the same section, the main -- the same body in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like you to point --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again I object to leading, Mr. President. That last question was leading, and what applies in examination-in-chief in my respectful submission applies in re-examination as well. utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will put that differently, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.text: Witness, you now have a symbol which is not that clear. I would like you to put your pointer more to the left of the map. It is a red symbol, and it's in a circle which is also in a type of an ellipsis. It is slightly above the "K". Stop, stop.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle of the screen, upwards to the left, could you put your pointer more to the left, to the left, Witness. That's the right. Further up. Further up. Stop.

utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.text: You've got a symbol here and there is something inscribed in the middle, and two red marks, to the right and to the left of what is inscribed. Could you have a look at these two red inscriptions, Witness. Can you tell us what these two red symbols correspond to on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This indicates the firing position of a brigade artillery group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you repeat your answer, please. I am not sure -- that's fine. That's fine. When you say an artillery group, Witness, what do the two symbols represent? What do they correspond to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The red symbol indicates the weapons which are part of the brigade artillery group. In this particular case it is 120-millimetre mortar and a Howitzer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, since you mentioned a 120-millimetre mortar, could you indicate, could you point to the symbol that represents a 120-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, the witness pointed to the symbol which is to the left of the marking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, I am assuming that the other symbol represents -- could you please tell us what it represents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It represents a Howitzer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could you now have a look at the key on this map. I can provide you with a copy.

utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, according to your military experience --

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, could you repeat that, please, Witness. Could you repeat -- could you read the line at the bottom.

utterances.text: In the third line it says: "contact line the 21st of August 1994."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Given your military experience and with regard to the date on which this map was produced, what can you tell us about the last date, when you read the text, when there are modifications or when additions were made to this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when one is adding something or modifying a map in chronological order, as this appears to be the case, does one take into consideration all the necessary elements, that is my question? utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll reformulate my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, could we have a look at the upper part of the map which is to the right, just slightly to the right of the map. That's fine, thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, stop. Thank you. Could you point to the zone where the village of Mrkovici is on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrkovici. Thank you.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Witness pointed to the map --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in immediate surroundings of Mrkovici that you have just pointed to, can you see when background of the -- whether there is a symbol in the background of the Mrkovici area which represents an artillery position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President, on the basis that this, again, does not arise out of cross-examination. Not to mention the fact that it is leading.

Not primarily because this all has been covered by the cross-examination, but since the Chamber deems it fair that if it orders the production of a map, that if there is any additional question to be put to the witness in this respect, that the Defence is allowed to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would be grateful if you could indicate at this stage whether the Prosecution will have an opportunity to ask this witness questions about the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are new questions, and I gave you the reasons why we allowed the Defence to examine the witness on these issues. And since this is more or less examination-in-chief rather than re-examination, the Prosecution will have an opportunity put questions in respect of those issues covered by the Defence at this very moment. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. Mr. President, I want to state the following: The Prosecution produced the map for incident 5, that's this map here, and we want to clarify matters by referring to a bigger map. So I think this is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you carefully examine this map and to go a few kilometers towards the rear, to the north of Mrkovici, have a look there and I would like to ask you the same question for the area which is a few kilometers to the north of the Mrkovici area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further up. And my question is the same one, to the north of Mrkovici, is there a firing -- is there an artillery position that might be symbolised on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I would now like you to have a very careful look at this map. And could you point to the following names: Greda, if you can find it.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness pointed to the lower right-hand corner to the largest rectangle in the zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just have to check a name. Just a second. And could you please point further to the right, could you point to the place called Barice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now show the witness the document that we had a look at yesterday, and which concerns the Markale incident number 5, and then we will have a break afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the well-known maps that we saw yesterday, and which regard the incident number 5.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can't remember the number offhand. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It was inappropriate to mention the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you should have referred to a number of an incident, but to nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. I apologise. That's right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you recognise the map on -- to your right? I am simply asking whether you can recognise it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Witness, could you take your pointer and indicate Greda on this map, and point to this map which concerns incident number 5.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has indicated an area outside of the dotted lines to the right of the dotted line. Mr. President, I think we could have the break now.

utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Should be dealt with with everyone standing, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Except that Mr. President, what I wanted is to have the rule respected. Considering that this will be tendered into evidence, the rule has always been that the parties will not leave with what will be given as proof, as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have considered this and I -- let me just...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where as a general rule the chain of custody would require not to give such a map out of hand, the -- just as the Defence can have the map for discussing with General Galic, the Chamber is convinced that it is such an effort to copy such a map, that we do not think that the parties could do that within the next half hour. So there is in this specific moment not a risk that anything would happen or that it would be altered. That would be easily detected, and apart from that, to replace it by another map of similar size is almost unimaginable. We will adjourn until 10 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be brought into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to go back, not to the maps that we looked at, that we examined, but on the points that were raised in cross-examination of yesterday, and to do with the area of Sedrenik and what we call the Sharpstone feature. Do you remember that we spoke of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know -- I withdraw that. What can you tell us about the frequency of fighting in this area, first, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "on a daily basis," Witness, can you tell us give us an indication, not on the frequency, but of the scale of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Relevance in the sense that it doesn't arise out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes. Well, perhaps the witness could take off his earphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that might not be enough. Could you ask, please, the witness to leave the courtroom for a second. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. President, we have a number of incidents that are to do with the area of Sedrenik, and that are to do also with the sharp rock feature. During the cross-examination Mr. Ierace questioned this witness for a long time about the position of the red circle, the position of the troops and so on. Now, what the Defence would like to be able to prove is that every day, including the dates of the incidents number 8, number 3, which were the sniper Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. incidents, there were frequent combats, that is, there was frequent fighting because this was to do with the question of stray bullets. Because the witness told us with a lot of precision that the range was 4 or 5.000 metres. So there would be exchanging of fire, and more there are such exchanges, more there is a chance of stray bullets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is my recollection right when the intensity of combat, one of the examples specifically dealt with on the 24th of July was raised in chief, and that the matter of stray bullets, I remember a question, what would be the effect of a stray bullet, would it be any different from a bullet that would hit the object targeted were dealt with relatively extensively in chief. So I take it that the -- that in cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- It was an issue that was not newly raised. I will allow you one or two questions in this respect. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it wasn't raised at all in cross-examination, stray bullets; and secondly, this witness said that the first time he went to that area was after the conflict when he drove along a road near it. So the proper basis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, that is the intensity of fighting in that area might not be exactly the same as going with your car to a road which ends somewhere at -- somewhere where -- I don't know for what reason it ends there, but it ends there. Let's -- we have to keep in mind that what do we lose by allowing one or two questions, and what do we lose by a fierce fight on this kind of question. But, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, self-restrictions, of course, a thorough examination of whether the issue was raised in chief would be highly appreciated by the Chamber. Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. So that we can advance, could we please put back on the ELMO P3278. This is to do with incident number 3 to start with. It is the map that we know well by now, and also, Mr. President, in order to save time, what we would like to indicate now would be valid, mutatis mutandis, for incident number 8 which is of the same character from the technical point of view. Thank you, Madam Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please focus on this map that you can see. Could you please put the pointer or point with a pointer on the red circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has done just that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you put it below the green line, wavy green line and follow the light green lines.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. You can follow it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please indicate with the pointer in which direction where exchanges of fire happening on -- from both sides, when they were taking place in this area?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The basis hasn't been laid for that question given the witness's evidence as to when he first went to that part and where he was stationed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please have the basis laid, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, according to your knowledge of the area and your personal experience, did you know in which direction were soldiers firing, those who were defending at the same time the light green line and also the area which is located around the dark green line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you then indicate in which direction where exchanges of fire were taking place? Could you do it with a pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness first indicated from the light green undulated area, a certain number of directions going more or less to the north, and then from the other direction as well, and the same thing from the upper area, but this time with the firing or shooting going in the southerly direction, southern easterly direction, and southern westerly direction. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that doesn't properly describe the actions of the witness with the pointer. In relation to the firing from the dark green line to the light green line, the action of the witness stopped around the area of the light green line. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first ask you, because I asked you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to lay a foundation, and would you ask the witness whether he knew anything. Looking at the red circle, during the conflict, have you been at that position? First of all, were you ever stationed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever visit that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How often did you visit that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't tell you exactly. On several occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, is "several" less than ten, more than ten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More than ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: More than ten. Under what circumstances did you visit that position? What --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This position is located approximately at the linking point between my battalion and the neighbouring battalion. So these visits happened so that we would establish closer links, better connection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you were at these positions, was there combat activity going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometimes, yes, there was; sometimes there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this is the foundation the Prosecution asked for. That's different from just asking, "do you know it?" That is not a foundation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, now on the basis of the foundation that we have just been given --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in brackets the Prosecution raised the point of my description, but I believe that my description was correct. Do I have to do it again for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you ask the witness again. It was not quite clear to me what he pointed at, so, therefore, whether it is correct --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the basis of your knowledge, what we are interested in are the shooting, the firing during fighting that came originating from the dark green area. Could you, again, point with the pointer and show us the direction of these shooting, as you have already done so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the witness has indicated Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. several areas of firing, going from the north to the south, from the north to the south-east, and from the north to the south-west. For the south-east, I think I could say that that direction was Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, the weapons that were used during combat, during fighting, were these weapons -- no, I withdraw that. What were the weapons used during this fighting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is minded to allow this, and in any event on the basis of what already is permitted, I seek the opportunity for further cross-examination in relation to it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what were the weapons used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Infantry weapons that I have already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please remind us the range, the ranges of these weapons, very briefly, and general.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The range of the weapons depending on the type, that would be from 4 to 5.000 metres and some of them up to 8.000, even.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you didn't give the answer to my first question which was the following: You spoke about the frequency of the combat on a daily basis. Now, what was in terms of scale, can you tell us something more about the engagements and the fighting, the scale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intensity, the scale differed, depending on the situation, specifically in this area, in the greater area here, there were high intensity fighting and combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, according to your personal experience, when there is ratherly considerable high intensity fighting, what about the possibility of what we call stray bullets? What is the probability that they will occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a high probability of that occurring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since these maps are not very precise in terms of scale, according to your experience of the locations, could you tell us what was the distance between the red point number 3, could you please find it with the pointer on the map to your right. Just below. Below. Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we can't see it. Just a moment. Here it is, yes. So between this point and the red circle, what was the distance, more or less?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly on this map. I can't quite find my bearings, but up to 2.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, you see a second red dot which is to the north of the dot that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the witness is pointing to it. This is the dot next to number 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between this dot and the circle, between this point and the circle what was the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this it would be perhaps some several hundred metres closer to the red circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you tell us since you testified yesterday that the green line wasn't precisely your position, could you indicate what is, as much as you can recall, the position of your lines in this area, that is, to the north of the map that you were presented with? Could you please indicate that with a pointer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the technical booth, could you please help us to have a look at the entire map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you understood my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you do that again, please. Could you retrace it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part that I know for certain, I can't indicate it here, but I will show you this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to simplify matters, we are going to provide copies of this map, black and white copies, and this will be Exhibit number -- now, perhaps, I need the assistance of Madam Registrar. D17 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the witness can use a black felt tip and mark the line as it appears. And we would like to mention that this map is only a copy of what we were provided with by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- And on this light modification has been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Mr. Ierace, you said you would need only a couple of minutes. Please proceed, and conclude your examination now in a couple of minutes. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't follow, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am sorry. I am sorry. Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I have to apologise. It was just -- you see how equal the parties are for this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will certainly need a lot more than a few minutes. The reason I rose to my feet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- Is to seek access to the map. Because as I understood as what my learned colleague just said, it is not a photocopy of the map which is presently on the ELMO. So I would like to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I could just see the both of them --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Mr. President, it is a photocopy of this map, but at the time we introduced a modification that one of the witnesses had made, one of the witnesses that had been heard, and it was nothing else. It was a standard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it is a... Mr. Ierace, the map produced now is a map without the marking of the witness, but on it the marking of someone else, but same position, same type of marking. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a black felt tip and as far as you can remember this, could you please trace what, in your opinion, could have been the positions, what the line could have been in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: "What could have been the positions" that is unacceptable, Mr. President, in my respectful submission. That is not reliable evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I said what the lines could be, that's what I said in French. That means that I don't know what that could be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What the -- it would assist the Chamber, although it is marked perhaps on other maps as well, where the positions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the purpose of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is not the language of your question. Could you please mark where the positions actually were as you indicated before on the coloured map. Yes, would you please do it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you stopped above the Grdonj inscription. Why didn't you continue to the left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I am not sure. That wasn't my zone any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace. Further cross-examination by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before you mark the map -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before interrupting Mr. Ierace, I would like to stress that I have to leave, I have to go to Geneva about 12.00 or 12.15. I hope this will not be a discourtesy on my part, if I do so, with your permission, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it then as always the full responsibility is in the hands of Ms. Pilipovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you marked this map you were twice asked to indicate with a pointer where the front line was. On both of those occasions, you passed your pointer through the circle. Do you agree with that, that that's what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked to show the directions in which fire was exchanged, if I am not mistaken. I apologise. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. You were asked to indicate the positions, the position of the front line, and on both occasions you passed your pointer through the circle in response to that question, and I will repeat, on two separate occasions. Do you agree that that's what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when it came time to drawing the line, you didn't do that. You didn't pass the line through the circle. Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the trench line followed the path that I marked and here forces were present in this circle, that is not in dispute, but it was a prominent point. We soldiers call it "combat security."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that your forces were present in the circle, but the trenches were behind the circle; is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The line, the main defence line followed the path that I indicated, and in this part we had a point which was a prominent combat security point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was at that prominent combat security point? What exactly was there in that position, exactly, let's say in mid-1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It consisted of a certain number of men who were first engaged in fighting, who observe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Observers, men engaged in fighting. What weaponry did they have at that point in mid-1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing in particular. People would be designated from the units, so for a certain period of time they are taken to the front here, part of them were taken to the front here, and part of them were taken to the front -- at this position, the people changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was what weaponry they had. You give a lengthy answer, but not about the weaponry. Could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they had the same weapons that the other men in the unit had, so automatic rifles, light machine-guns, it depended on the man, the soldier, who was there at the time. It depended on the weapon he had been issued with in the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the nature of the facility at that point? Was it a dugout, a trench? What was there in the way of protection at that particular point, that observation point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trenches had been dug.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. I don't think that this type of question arises from what we -- from the subjects that we addressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have been rather liberal to the Defence. Prosecution may ask these questions specifically since the Defence asked to draw the line on this map. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that it was an observation point --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the trenches had been dug, it was an observation point. What optics did the observers use, binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say it was an observation point. It wasn't an observation post, but part of the combat assignment of the unit was combat action and combat security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, it was a forward position, you've told us, beyond the trenches, and in relation to your evidence yesterday, on a high point, on the escarpment. It was used for observation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You observe from all positions. A soldier observes from all positions, including this one, but it wasn't there for this particular purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It overlooked Sedrenik, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of it, roughly speaking. I can't indicate it exactly here, but a small part of the periphery of Sedrenik could be seen, and this part here is a forest area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sedrenik was beyond the front line, wasn't it, beyond --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the sake of the transcript, Mr. Ierace should say where the witness mentioned the presence of forest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness pointed below an area just below the red circle, a bit right, more to the north of where it is written "Sedam Suma." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I withdraw the previous question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you travelled to the observation point, how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is an interconnecting trench in one part, and since there is a forest behind, this part was sheltered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the road behind the trenches used for providing -- for supplying that part of the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't necessary to use it for any particular kind of supplies because people would be changed. They were there for a certain period of time, but I don't know exactly because this didn't concern my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The road was used, wasn't it, by the SRK forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand the question. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The road behind the front lines was used by vehicles belonging to the SRK; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the road through Mrkovici, it was used, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember yesterday I asked you if you had ever been on that road, and you said "no." Do you remember being asked that question and giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will read you the question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the witness is confused. Could we ask the witness to indicate on the map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we first -- we are not going to interfere at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, on my transcript it is page 78 of yesterday's LiveNote commencing at line 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, have you ever travelled on that road ever? And at that point you had your pointer on the road. You said: "Yes, after the Dayton Agreement." Next question: "All right, I take it you did not travel on that road before the war?" Answer: "No." "Q. And when you went there after the Dayton Agreement to the right of the road -- withdraw that -- did you leave the road and walk around the area at the end?" There was then an interruption. The question was repeated and you said: "No, I only drove down it. "Q. Why did you drive down it," and I think you said "Mrkovici, because it was necessary." Do you remember I asked you those questions yesterday and you gave those answers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, sir, but right now obviously you don't know the story and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. we are not referring to the same road at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you had your pointer, when I asked you those questions, on the road which appears behind where you have marked the confrontation line, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not precise, this entire series of questions. I object because there are several roads behind the trench line and this could have created confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if Mr. Piletta-Zanin cares to consult the transcript, I think he would be left in no doubt that the pointer was on the appropriate road, if he doesn't remember it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you for the suggestion that was made to me. With regard to this, the witness's answer was that he was speaking about the road that goes towards Mrkovici, and we can see that this is not the one that Mr. Ierace was thinking of, but it was the other one which goes in the direction of the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have the evidence of yesterday clearly in my mind. I have the evidence of today clearly in my mind. There might be confusion as to the roads. So, therefore, Mr. Ierace, I don't think it will greatly assist the Chamber to continue on this specific issue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I suggest to you that yesterday you conveyed the impression in your answers that you had not been to this area during the conflict. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that is correct. I wasn't there all the time, but occasionally I did go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
