utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown D1789. Might the ELMO zoom in on the part of the front line marked by the witness, if that could be centred on the screen. Yes. A bit too far, I think. Yes, that's good. A bit further. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember yesterday I asked you to mark the front line beyond your area of responsibility. Do you remember I asked you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember that at my request you placed a dash across the front line to indicate where your responsibility ended, and you then proceeded with a blue pen to show us where the front line was, as far as you could recollect. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to the area that you marked. Place your pointer on that extension.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness does that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now point to Grdonj on the same map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does Grdonj appear -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness now points to Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now point to the road that was behind the trenches at Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you unable to do it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your view, are you pointing at the road you were asked to point at? I understand --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The road I am pointing at now goes from Grdonj to Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Point again to Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the north-east of the pointer, indeed due north of the pointer, do you see a dead-end road, approximate -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You now point to the dead-end road. Please keep the pointer still at the dead end of the road. Thank you. Sir, that is the road which appears in the map which you have just marked behind the trenches; do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I suggest to you that the front line, as you have marked it on this map, bears no resemblance to the front line as you have marked it at the invitation of the Defence a few moments ago on map 4, number 3. Do you agree or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't fully agree with that since the maps are different, and the scales used are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. DP20, what Mr. Ierace is asking you that where you marked on the map only recently the trenches or the defence line south of the dead-end road, that on the other map the defence line of your army is close to Barice and north of that dead-end road. And he asks you whether you agree that there is a difference between the lines you've drawn on the map we have on the screen and the line you have drawn on the other map at the request of Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you went to that part of the front lines, I think at least ten times. Sir, I suggest to you that sniping was carried out from that area. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that isn't so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you, indeed, civilians were shot from that part of the front line. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that from that area or from any part of the front line that I know, civilians were not targeted, but whether they were hit, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object. I believe that the question of snipers has never been phrased, has never been asked at any point during examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you wish me to respond to that, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, first of all, in examination-in-chief we had evidence as to the range of rifles, we were told of the significance of the two dates of the documents shown to the witness, and you might recall what I said about that in the absence of the witness yesterday, the significance of those dates. In re-examination, if one could call it that, rather than re-examination in chief, Mr. Piletta-Zanin has asked this witness as to the distance on this map between the circle and point 3, the direction of fire and so on. The Defence has in all but name asked multiple questions on sniping, and now the reason I ask it snow is for the first time we hear from the witness that he was there in fact there at the relevant period, that is, the area of the circle. It wasn't brought out in chief. It wasn't given in cross-examination, but left to re-examination. And that's why it is appropriate to now cross-examine this witness about sniping from that point during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question has been answered, meanwhile. The objection is unfounded. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you asked a few moments ago about where the firing was from the SRK front line in that area, and you indicated towards the south. Of course, the direction of fire, if the ABiH front line was being targeted, was downwards from the escarpment, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of the trenches, of the BH Army trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In other words, if troops on your side were firing at the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. ABiH positions, their rifles, their machine-guns, were pointed down, not parallel with the earth, but down the escarpment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, always in the direction of the enemy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you understand there were civilians living in Sedrenik during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not informed about that. Logically it would be that considering that Sedrenik was close to the front line, this area should have been evacuated. It shouldn't contain any civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Leaving aside what should or should not have happened, logically, did you not understand that there were civilians living in Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. What do you mean "logically"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was obvious to you, that's what I mean, sir, that civilians were living in Sedrenik during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in any way. It wasn't obvious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has anyone ever informed you before today that there were civilians living in Sedrenik during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the first time that it has been suggested to you, that there were civilians living in Sedrenik at the time of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President. I object. The question, the way it is phrased, is much too general. Sedrenik is a wide area, and it would be good to have it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Said with precision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The reference to Sedrenik has been used several times. It -- the question may be put as such to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I take it today is the first time that that's even been suggested to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less so, because I never discussed with anyone before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you surprised to hear it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In a way, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you went to that trench area and looked out over Sedrenik, do I take it that you believed that the only people below you were combatants, the only people in Sedrenik; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I, therefore, take it that anyone you saw, as far as you were concerned, was a lawful target, someone you were entitled to shoot and kill in Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was watching, I never saw anyone else but soldiers in uniform and that not in Sedrenik, I never saw anyone in Sedrenik, but next to the front line, closer to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say you only ever saw persons who were soldiers. Do I understand you to be saying that you never saw anyone in Sedrenik, not even soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sedrenik, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see vehicles travelling through Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this area, Spicasta Stijena, one has panoramic view taking in, not only Sedrenik, but also the eastern part of the city, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see more the opposite side, opposite the mount of Trebevic, that would be the other side of the Miljacka river, all the way across there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you see everything in between, don't you, including the old part of the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not quite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you see any part of the Old City from there, according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see the lower part -- I don't quite know. I can't tell you quite precisely which area I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me it was important for you to know what areas were occupied perhaps by civilians and what areas definitely were not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but at that time I couldn't have had such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's be clear on this. You say that at that time you couldn't have had such information. Did you have information to the effect that there were no civilians in Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the information come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the people who followed that. They didn't see any civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did it come from your superiors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, from the soldiers who were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the soldiers stationed at that part informed you that there were no civilians in Sedrenik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I take it they told you that they shot at anyone they saw; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. They may not have said that to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object. This type of questions is very subjective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Conditional hypothesis and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't know that there is a high degree of hypothesis, Mr. President, but the question has been answered. I am happy to move on to my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you came to the trenches, they told you there are no civilians in Sedrenik. It followed from that, did it not, as a matter of simple logic, that anyone in Sedrenik, as far as they were concerned, was a proper target; is that not correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Why isn't it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because you can tell a soldier and a civilian apart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you -- I withdraw that. From where you were stationed, did you ever shoot at soldiers with a rifle or a machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I went there on a different business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anywhere on your part of the front line did you personally ever shoot at soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever shoot at someone you believed to be a soldier who was not in a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not? Because the opportunity never presented itself or because you preferred to only shoot at persons wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only fired at people who were in or within --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. I believe that the term "to prefer" is not proper the way that this has been said, "preferred" I believe that is a completely shocking, the way that it is negatively been used.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, why did you not shoot at persons who weren't wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have the need to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean that you never saw anyone on the other side of the confrontation line within range at any stage during the conflict who wasn't wearing a uniform; is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had seen someone, an adult let's say, a male, not in uniform and within range on the other side of the confrontation line, in your opinion would they have been a lawful target?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he is in the area --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object. I object. There is no precision in this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... In court having regard to the last two or three objections by my learned colleague, that the witness not be in court during the expression for the reason of the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't give you my explanation for the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... The question was not precise enough, and the objection is denied because the precision of the question does not oppose to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I? May I tell you exactly what I mean in the absence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am happy to rephrase the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any orders to not shoot people who weren't in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Relatively often we received orders not to fire at civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, listen to the question carefully: Did you ever receive an order to not shoot individuals who were not in uniform? I will rephrase it. Did you ever receive orders to only shoot people who were in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only people in uniform and with weapons, bearing weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So your orders were that even if a person was in uniform, if they weren't bearing weapons, then you were not to shoot them; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right. I think, generally speaking, a person either in uniform or with weapons or with both. For me, that is a soldier, that is something from the opposing side, the enemy, who should be fired at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever receive those orders in writing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see such a written order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think the answer was yes. I haven't heard the translation. Did you say, yes, that you have seen such a written order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean your battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it at the battalion command which means that the battalion commander received this written order from the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in relation to this order, if you saw a person in the distance who was not wearing a uniform and who was not clearly carrying a weapon, would you have shot at that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I come back to the view from Spicasta Stijena. You've told us that you understood there were no civilians in Sedrenik. You've told us from the same position you could see the city. Where did you draw the line? In other words, what part of that view did you regard to be bereft of civilians, and what part to contain civilians, if any part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't divide it in terms of sections of view. I can say that next to the BH Army line, that was without civilians, that is how I considered it. And then further on away from the defence line of the BH Army, I think that that area contained civilians. That will be the central part of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the earlier map be placed on the ELMO, that is, I think it is the one for incident 3, the colour version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember that you were asked questions about the distance from the circle to a point marked 3 on the map and you said that it was up to 2 kilometers away, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where that point 3 was, do you regard that -- I withdraw that. Was the position of point 3 where you believed there to be civilians, and where you believed there to be no civilians? I think you now have the map in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is part of the area of the BH Army defence and consider that there were no civilians there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to be clear on this, I am asking you about the point on the map, perhaps you can point to it, which is marked with the number "3."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please follow the line south-west from that square to the red dot. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What about south-east, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am sorry, south-east. Thank you. The witness now has the pointer on the red dot indicated as number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in a civilian area or a noncivilian area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is the area of the defence line and that there were no civilians there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the red dot above it, please point to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same, that you believed that to be in a noncivilian area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your belief is based on what you were told by the troops who were in the area of the red circle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown the large map opened at the area on which he was re-examined, that's the coloured map which has come from the Defence, the very large one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on this map we see various symbols for artillery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you understand this to be a corps working map as in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps working map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand it to be a working map for the corps staff, and if you have any doubt about that, perhaps the map can be opened up and the witness shown the top left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am not sure if the witness has already seen that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you earlier seen the heading of this map, its title?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not. This is the first time I am having a look at this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If very quickly the map could be opened up so we could view the top left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please read out the title of the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The working map of the headquarters" -- do I have to read on? "Started on the 1st of the July 1994 and further on" there is nothing more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reference to headquarters, do you understand that to be the corps headquarters rather than a brigade headquarters or a battalion headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering this size and the area covered, I think this is the headquarters of the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the symbols we see for artillery, that is artillery for the brigade or for the corps, not the battalion; is that correct? Not the battalion level.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, for instance, we don't see on this map 120-millimetre mortars which were held by the battalions, do we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here you can see the mortar indicated 120-millimetre over there. I don't know which unit it was part of, to whom it belonged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please place your pointer on the part of the map that you are referring to when you answered that last question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this here, this is the symbol for the mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Leave your pointer in that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, the witness indicates a part of the map to the north of Sarajevo where there appears a more or less as cigar shaped box with red symbols and some Cyrillic writing in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please read the writing in the middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brag. B-R-A-G.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It stands for "brigade" doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gate, artillery group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words that indicates brigade artillery, not battalion artillery, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you earlier said that here we see a mortar, that's a brigade armament, not a battalion armament, isn't it, or a corps armament -- I withdraw that. It is a brigade armament because that's what it says, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we don't see on this map mortars attached to battalions, only brigade mortars and corps mortars or corps artillery, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the battalion had mortars at Mrkovici, we wouldn't see it on this map, would we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the battalion ones are not placed in unless they were part of the artillery group of the brigade, which is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely. Now, the point of this map is to assist the corps headquarters in understanding the front lines over the entire area of responsibility for the corps, and its assets at a brigade and corps level; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what would you say was the distance from the symbol that you pointed to earlier, the 120-millimetre mortars at the brigade level from the centre of Sarajevo, just approximately? Are we talking 50 kilometers, 20 kilometers, or perhaps 10 kilometers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you, to answer this question. I do not wish to give you any incorrect answers. I don't have any means to measure, and I don't know this terrain that well so that I would be able to give an answer from my experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, not that well, but you did spend the entire war slightly to the right of that entire area, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And firstly, the symbol on the right-hand side, what does that indicate? Mortar on the left, what's on the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness answered that question already, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The artillery and mortars are at Poljine according to the map, in that area, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Poljine is less than 20 kilometers from the centre of Sarajevo, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The heavy weapons exclusion agreement, have you ever heard of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did that come into operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly because I was not much involved to do with this agreement because I was in the infantry, and this agreement was to do with the artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to move you very quickly around the circumference to the right. Could you please use your pointer to indicate lines if they appear that denote the boundaries of the individual brigades, in particular, the northern line for your brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence objects. Bearing in mind the answer of the witness to the questions that proceeded this question, which is yesterday, and I would like to, therefore, object. Considering the witness has earphones, there shouldn't be any problems. Your Honour, perhaps the witness could take his earphones so that we can -- I can explain the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't agree that the witness should remain in court for the objection, even if they don't understand English entirely. But I do press the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is not quite clear to me. So I have to ask the witness to leave the court for a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there were questions yesterday asked by my learned colleague of the witness DP20 in terms of the brigade lines. And now I can't be very precise, but I know for sure that the witness said that he didn't know the lines of the brigade because he -- although he did know the lines of the battalion. Yesterday when we discussed the map and when the witness was marking on the map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I feel that there might be some confusion. I take it, Ms. Pilipovic, you are referring to the confrontation line of the brigade and where the witness stopped and said "I do not know much further to the west." Is that what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. Yes, he said he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that your question is about the northern boundaries of the brigade, Mr. Ierace, is that correct, so not the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there seems to be some confusion. You are referring to something different. The questions yesterday are not the same subject as the question Mr. Ierace is putting to the witness at this very moment. But perhaps, Mr. Ierace, the question could be put more clearly because if Ms. Pilipovic is confused, the witness must be confused as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, precisely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness had indicated the appropriate marker by the time Madam Pilipovic was making her objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I missed it then. Can we first ask the witness to come into the courtroom again and perhaps you ask him to do it again, because sometimes I have to pay attention to more than one person

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to future objections it doesn't assist that the witness takes off his headphones given that he speaks the same language as Madam Pilipovic, unless Madam Pilipovic makes her objection in a non-Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I never asked you to learn any French and I'll never ask Ms. Pilipovic to learn any other language as well. Could the witness be please brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think this comment wasn't appropriate, the one made by my colleague. I am just trying to avoid any difficult situations, since we have been in difficult situations before. I am quite aware of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It certainly was not necessary. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just on that, Mr. President, I did not mean anything critical of my friend at all. There might be a misunderstanding as to the reason I made that observation. It related to any future objection, and the pointlessness of removing headphones, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the Chamber accepts that Mr. Ierace did not want to express any nasty feeling and Ms. Pilipovic neither did, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please point to the boundary as it appears on this map of your brigade on the northern side of the city.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't point to it because this is the period when the battalion was part of the 3rd Sarajevo Infantry Brigade. In fact -- well, I apologise. To the north, that means in the depth, if I have understood you correctly. Or are you referring to the ring around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just before you left the courtroom, you pointed to a line. Would you please place your pointer back on that line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't point to anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see on the map there are some red broken lines that intersect the front line in the north-east of the city, in the vicinity of the portion of the front line that you had responsibility for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Does that indicate the boundaries -- do those lines indicate the boundaries between the brigades of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these are the boundaries between the battalions from within a brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there lines on the map that indicate the brigade boundaries? Sir, if it saves time, I am not trying to trick you, I suggest that you have made a mistake and that those lines indicate the brigade boundaries. If you look further along to the right, if you follow the confrontation lines, do you see the next such line is to the south of the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you want me to indicate, what I am to look at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am suggesting to you that those red broken lines are the boundaries of the brigades. In your case, we see the boundaries of your brigade of the Romanija Brigade. If you don't know that, please indicate that and we will move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is time for the break anyhow, Mr. Ierace. I think we will adjourn until 1.00. But could the map -- is the map -- the large map, is it somewhere here that I can have a closer look to it during the break. Yes. We will adjourn until 1.00. Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to be informed of when I can be provided with a copy of this map because I haven't been told yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Taken to the reproduction so that we can see what can be done today, is that correct, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I need only one minute for the map, yes. We will adjourn until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, a full copy of the map will be produced tomorrow. If there are specific parts you would like to have copied, but then only small parts, we can see what we can do this afternoon. But the full map will be copied by tomorrow. There will not be copies for the Prosecution. There'll be no copies for the Bench. The original is with the Registrar. But what could be done is to have copies on a disk so that we can consult them. But printing of these maps is extremely expensive, and, therefore, a copy of the map -- a printed copy of the map will be provided to the Defence who needs it for further preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could I make a suggestion, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The relevant part of the map, that is the part that shows Sarajevo, I imagine that wouldn't be expensive to have multiple copies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are talking about this part or perhaps the three or four portions, I take it that that can be done. It only problem is you easily damage such a map. And it is already put together, but we will see what can be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, finally what kind of copies will be made, perhaps they will be made of that copy still to be produced. But we will see what we can do and do it as good as possible. But tomorrow your full copy will be produced. Then, could the witness be brought into the courtroom again. Mr. Ierace, how much time would you still need because the Chamber would like to finish with the witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: About -- no longer than 10 minutes, Mr. President, probably not longer than that

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because we will have some questions so would you please try to be as efficient as possible. Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but could you tell me when the map will be ready tomorrow so that my associate can come to collect it and who should we report to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ask Ms -- ask the Registrar after the hearing because she doesn't know it now and we have to find out. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, might the witness be shown the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The portion that shows Sarajevo. Might I have access to the map? It might save some time. Mr. Usher, if I could have a look at the map. I will point out to Mr. Usher the parts I will be referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the map we see on the north of the city some boxes containing some blue writing, in particular, three boxes with writing. Would you please read what appears in the top left-hand box. And please Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. read it slowly. No, the box to the left of the pointer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness points to the top left box.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read it out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I am trying to, but I can't really do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not very clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read the writing in any of those three boxes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it says: "Security department."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you know that if there is any need to confer with General Galic, then it should be done at a low volume and you should --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The General only asked me if we could zoom into the photograph, into the -- if we could zoom in and perhaps zoom into this part and it might then be possible to read what it says. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. For the benefit of the transcript, we now have enlarged on the screen the top left blue box of the group of three north of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Security department," the first word I think or the first number, perhaps it is "2," perhaps it says "2010 men" but this in front of the letter "C" I am not sure whether I can make it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the interest of saving time, we will stop there. But do you agree that having regard to the lines connecting the boxes to other boxes on the ABiH side in Sarajevo, these boxes with blue writing appear to refer to places and facilities and military resources in Sarajevo on the ABiH side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would Mr. Usher please bring up on the map the second area I indicated I would be going to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you now see on the map and in particular on the screen an irregularly shaped, four-sided box with three letters and one number written inside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the transcript, this appears to the right of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to it with your pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we see four symbols in red. Could you tell us what each of those symbols depict? What type of military equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This isn't very clear to me. I can't say exactly, but they represent artillery, but I can't tell you what artillery pieces exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you please read the writing which we see in the box.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Kag," K-A-G, 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does Kag 1 stand for corps artillery group one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you now please take us to the third indicated area. A bit further down. The brown box. Thank you. If you could move it so we can see where the line going from the top left-hand corner of the brown box connects. Further. Further. Further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do we have here a box with some information and a line connecting that box to Lukavica? Please point to the line connecting the box.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And does that go to Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am showing this now, up to Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read what appears in the brown box, and whilst you read it, perhaps the ELMO can be adjusted so that the contents of the box are enlarged. Could you please read that out so that we can hear it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first word is "department for security." I am not sure that that's what it says, though. The second and third lines, I can't read them at all. The last line it says "IDO, Bijeli Vukovi, White Wolves." And the rest I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rather than read it on the screen, you might be able to read it right off the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Department for security and intelligence affairs, six to seven men." I can't decipher the second line and then it says, "IDO, Bijeli Vukovi, White Wolves, 60 men."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first word on the third line, can you decipher that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but it is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did "IDO" stand for, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reconnaissance and sabotage detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the White Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were members of the reconnaissance and sabotage detachment, and they were called the White Wolves, Bijeli Vukovi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they attached to a brigade or to the corps directly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They weren't part of my brigade. I think that they were attached to the corps, directly attached to the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were they called the White Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where this name came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you were a professional soldier in the JNA before the war commenced. Did the White Wolves exist in the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first hear of them, in what year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halfway through 1994, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what context did you hear of them, from whom and what was said or what did you read?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read anything about it, but there were rumours that there were such a unit which contained courageous men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I notice that you are smiling. Could you explain to us why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has nothing to do with this. When I said "the boys," this isn't really a military term. So I was smiling to myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You tell us that you heard rumours there were such a unit which contained courageous men. What did you understand that they did which required courage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everything that is done in the course of a war and which involves fighting, all sorts of activities require courage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you know what I mean, I am sure. What did you hear they did which either required courage or exemplified courage? What was it they did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well I heard that they were very successful in mounting a defence on the outer ring towards the Trnovo location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you heard of the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any connection between the White Eagles and the White Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. President. That concludes cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question since the witness has the map in front of him. Could he mark in the northern part of the map that we have spoken of, the Sedrenik area, could he mark, could he indicate where it tells us which brigade is there, if the name of the brigade is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It may be a matter of translation, but the English reads "could he mark the area." I would object to the map having any Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. marks put on it. But I notice the witness has the pointer. But perhaps my learned colleague --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I only wanted to him to indicate that northern part. Could we zoom in to see what formation was there, to see whether we can see on the screen. Can the witness see this. Further re-examination by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I was reserving to the northern part in blue, the Sedrenik area, what we can see on the blue circle in the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at the upper part of the map. Could we put the map a bit further up. No. Put it up so we can see the lower part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you just tell us when you answered the question as to what brigade it was, were you referring to the 2nd Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That was a blatantly leading question, quickly answered, before I had an opportunity to object to the question. And I don't see how that arose out of anything I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first see. Ms. Pilipovic, on the transcript, it appears that it said: "Sir, you tell us where referring to the 2nd Mountain Brigade, that is reading unless the witness said something about this before.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, he did, for certain. I can't check it in the transcript, but you could ask the witness whether he said this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what happened before, so I am very much aware that these kind of things happen. Did you before, Ms. Pilipovic asked you to confirm it, were you referring to the 2nd Mountain Brigade? Did you use these words already when they were not used yet by Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. But I can't say when, right now, when I was being examined by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace, you may -- the objection is -- Ms. Pilipovic says that the witness used these words before. We always can check in the transcript whether when there is any doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just at this stage, I am completely unaware of what the context was when it was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Neither am I. Well, the question has been put to the witness, has been answered by the witness, and if the objection needs further elaboration, we should rather do it when we have checked tapes. Yes. Yes, Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you. Ms. Pilipovic, I did understand --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I understood this. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. You said that not all the artillery positions are depicted in the big map, in that one. Did I understood -- understand you well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I didn't speak about it, but I can't really claim one way or the other because I didn't know about all of the positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Then I will ask you: Are they depicted, all the positions are depicted in the map in your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can repeat, sir: I cannot tell you whether all of the positions have been marked because I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Okay. My second question is the following, I think that you said already that but it is just for clarification: Is the 120-millimetre mortar an artillery or an infantry weapon or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Grdonj, do you remember the name, of course?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We mentioned it often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: What is that? Is it a is town, a settlement, a village, a field, is a hill? What is Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: It is a hill. Okay. Could this Exhibit 1490 -- 1790 be shown to the witness. I think that you said that from the red circle you could see Sedrenik only partially because there were some woods in the area. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a partially wooded area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Could you point to those woods, again, please, with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: With using the red pen, please, could you circle the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has one or more questions for you. JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Sir, I'd like to make sure that I understood you correctly. Yesterday at a question that was asked by the Defence, you answered -- and I am going to quote in English [In English] "Seven woods area part of the BH Army was deployed in that area." And you added [In English] "They used 82-millimetre mortar. So, if I understand you correctly in this area, the BH Army had 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So you said that they also had 120-millimetre mortars. What you meant, that these were not in this area, but elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] My second question is in relation to the impact. Do you remember on how many occasions you yourself were able to establish that there were mortar impacts of 120-millimetre mortars. You told us about the depth and the effects and the debris, the stabiliser and so on. And how many occasions did you personally see the impact or impacts? Impact or impacts of 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell you the exact number, because I really don't recall the exact number, but there were many. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] The reason I am interested is that you said your experts explained to you where the shots were coming from, where the fire was coming from, the direction and so on, and that it was also possible for them to establish and to differentiate between the calibres, when they saw impacts and when after they looked at impacts, which calibres caused these impacts. Who were these experts? Were they military experts? Were they ballistics experts or soldiers with experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, anyone with a little more experience looking at the crater, anyone can tell about the type of the mortar shell. The direction has to be established by experts who are artillery experts. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. And it is from these people that you had the information with respect to the calibres and the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. My last question is in relation to the following: If I understand you correctly, you used, partially at least, the weapons that belonged to the former JNA. As far as you know, this army, did it not have rifles with telescopes, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did have. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So you personally received these types of rifles in your sector, in your department, at least?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such rifles, but I would have to explain a little more, that it should be rectified that we didn't have -- how to do the rectification of these rifles, and they couldn't be used efficiently, nor did we have people who were trained to do this kind of shooting. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And in the observation post, the observation post marked with a red circle, if I understand correctly, this was an observation point, so it had a clear view which may have been a good point, a good location, to use these kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecutor said that this was observation point. I am just saying that this was just a trench belonging to the VRS. I don't know that this -- these weapons were used from this point. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have got a few questions for you as well. First of all, may the map be -- the large map, the large colour map be -- just keep it as it is. So, that's good. It doesn't even have to -- Did I understand you well that this map is of the same scale as the maps you used at the battalion level; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you told us what was the scale of this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One to 25.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You also told us that 5 millimeters, half a centimetre on this map, would be 250 metres in reality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is -- when I have half a centimetre on a map of 1 to 25.000, would that not result in 125 metres, rather than 250 metres? Let me put it the following way to you, 1 to 25.000, one metre is 120 metres. So, therefore, 25.000 centimetres would be 250 metres, therefore, half a centimetre, would be 125 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had rounded it up to one centimetre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My next question, but before putting the next question to you, I first ask the parties, is there any disagreement as to the scale of this map? I heard no further questions on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I can't indicate yet my position in relation to this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think the best thing would be to look at the map to make sure what the scale is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought you had been looking at the map for a considerable time. What was wrong, your calculation, or what you said about the scale, because they do not go together well? Is the scale a different one or was your calculation not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My calculation is incorrect. Because I said this thinking of 1 centimetre, and yet I was speaking, referring to half a centimetre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say the calculation is not correct, but 1 to 25.000 is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for this answer. You said something about the map as far as the weaponry was concerned. Let me first ask you: How many artillery positions would be in your area of responsibility? And I am specifically asking to artillery positions including mortars. How many would -- even if you would not know of all of them, of how many do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you're not sure or are you sure that these are all your artillery positions OR mortars?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for interrupting. Do you want to distinguish the period before or after the heavy weapons exclusion zone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No it is for my question. I am not making any -- I will give you -- when you answered that question about three positions, what time did you have in mind, during the whole of the conflict or first year, second year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking of the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The beginning --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and the second year? Did IT change or did it change when rules were given to put weaponry together, yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there was certain calibre weapons that had to be moved, they were taken out. What I was thinking not just because of that, because of the movements of the weapons. It is the same number, but positions were moved of the weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the positions would change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Including the positions of mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And up until that moment where the heavy weaponry had to be moved to a certain area outside, would there be always three mortar positions or would there be more or less or would that change? So I am not talking about the time where there were certain regulations in force as to have the heavy weaponry under control.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly it was the same number of positions, except that they changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. Last question is about when you said about how far weapons would reach from your positions at the front line, you gave numbers as high as, I think, 5.000 metres or 6.000 metres. What weaponry did you have in mind at that moment when you gave that answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP20 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking of the weapons 7.9 millimetre calibre, and the M-74 machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your answer --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: M-84 machine-guns, the interpreter corrects herself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. This concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you very much for having come far away and having showed all patience with us during the last few days. You've answered all the questions of the parties and of the Bench. I thank you again for coming and I wish that you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do the parties know we are not sitting tomorrow, we will not sit next Monday, we will sit on Tuesday and that should be in the afternoon as far as I understand. Then a number has been given to the large, coloured map that, that will be number C2. Yes, we are sitting in the afternoon, same courtroom. Since we are heading for a relatively long weekend, is there anything the parties would like to raise at this very moment? It seems to be not. I thank the interpreters and the technicians very much for their assistance and the cooperation because I stole, again, seven minutes of your time. We will adjourn until next Monday -- Tuesday.
